/LILIAN

GOOD MORNING!

Baltic Exchange Market Report 17 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2752 (-88)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4097 (-242)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2248 (-9)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1737 (7)
Baltic Handysize Index: 903 (-1)
CAPESIZE
The market ended the week on a distinctly subdued note, with rates extending their recent losses as limited enquiry and weakening sentiment across both basins weighed heavily on trading activity. The BCI 5TC declined by $2,196 to $37,156. The C5 index fell by $0.585 to $11.805, while C3 eased by $0.628 to $32.717, reflecting softer fundamentals in both the Pacific and Atlantic. The Pacific lacked any meaningful momentum, with just one major C5 miner active during the day, resulting in very thin trading and little opportunity for owners to resist lower levels. Fixtures were reported around $11.70-$11.75 for C5, underlining the softer tone as the week drew to a close. In the Atlantic, conditions continued to deteriorate from both South Brazil and West Africa into China, while the North Atlantic also remained under pressure. Trading activity was limited, with offers for index-dates on C3 heard around $33.00, or marginally below, against bids near $31.50, highlighting the persistent gap between owners’ expectations and charterers’ ideas. With activity fading into the weekend and sentiment remaining cautious across both basins, the market closes the week firmly on the defensive.
PANAMAX
As expected a quiet end to the week, especially as yesterday had also petered out. The North Atlantic remained tight on the nearby positions, with Owners in no hurry to fix, and it was a similar story in the South with reported trades having been concluded earlier in the week, although brokers commented arrival upto 20th August remained strong. The Asian routes were fairly flat today with most content to roll over into next week with Australian minerals, NoPAc grains and Indonesian coal all benefitting from some Owners reluctance to ballast with the current uncertainty in the Middle East. The Akira (81,782 2019) Shanwei 25 July was said to have fixed a trip via Australia with coal to China at $19,000 to unnamed Charterers and Sea Kudos was linked to the Nord Draco (84,694 2014) CJK 15-17 July for a round voyage via EC Australia at a peculiar rate of $18,888. The 5TC average finished the week down $80 at $20,236, very close to last weeks close of $20,273.
SUPRAMAX
A gentle slide into the weekend, the day started quietly and nothing seemed to change. The 11TC average was up again closing the week at $21,960 with a rise of $93 today, driven by the Asian market which continued it steady rise throughout the week, mainly due to increased activity with no noticeable imbalance between supply and demand. The Atlantic was more active at the end of the week which bodes for next week, especially with more North American trades being concluded. The NM Cherry Blossom (60,494 2015) prompt Barranquilla went on subjects for a trip Itaqui intention coal to Oldendorff at $22,500 and TMC placed the Cecilie F (63,425 2024) open Wilmington 20 July on subjects delivery New Orleans for a grains trip to the Continent at $31,000.
There was also talk of the Josco Shengzhou (64,250 2022) open Christobal 23 July being on subjects with Seastar for a petcoke cargo from New Orleans to India in the very high $30,000’s, however a source commented that the Charterer had been bidding well below this level previously.
HANDYSIZE
The week wrapped up with a typically slow finish, as limited activity emerged to shift market dynamics. Overall Atlantic sentiment remained largely unchanged from the previous day with the Continent and Mediterranean continuing to display steady activity and a broadly balanced cargo-to-tonnage position. In the South Atlantic and US Gulf activity remained sluggish, with elevated tonnage counts and a lack of fresh demand contributing to a slightly softer trend in rates. Meanwhile the Asian market closed the week on a firmer tone with sources noting slightly tighter tonnage, partly due to typhoon-related delays, and expectations of a healthy market in the coming week. The 7TC average closed the day down by $9 to settle at $16,261.

Atlantic
The Efficiency OL (37,130 2010) open Rio Haina 15 July was placed on subjects for a trip from SW Pass to WC Central America at $18,000. The Aurora Vega (34,372 2011) open Maracaibo 15 July was placed on subjects via NC South America to Belfast with coal at $19,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The Singan (33,953 2020) open West Australia was fixed for a trip to China with alumina at $26,000, although further details were lacking.

Market Fundamentals
BHP Production Report

In BHP’s q2 production report, the company announced total iron ore production was up 5.2 Mt, quarter-on-quarter to 76.8 Mt (100% basis). West Australian Iron ore (WAIO) production rose 5.1 Mt from quarter ending 31 March to 74.8 Mt, while Samarco operations edged 0.1 Mt higher to 2.0 Mt. In FY25/26 (Jul-Jun) total production climbed 1.9 Mt year-on-year to a record 264.7 Mt, achieving FY26 guidance of 258-269 Mt, with increases from both WAIO (+0.3 Mt to 256.9 Mt) and Samarco (+1.6 Mt to 7.8 Mt).

In June, BHP also approved a ~$900m investment for the Ministers North project in Pilbara, expected to produce ~20 Mtpa of high-grade Brockman ore once ramped up, and support more than 305 Mtpa of sustained production, with the first ore expected in the FY29.

Trading Commentary
Cape
A quiet end to the week for Cape paper, reacting off a weaker physical market and another negative index print in the morning session, before late buy interest pushed the majority of the curve back to flat. The Aug contract was sold down to lows of 31350, before a series of better bids throughout the afternoon saw the contract close marginally up on the day, at 32300. Sep opened the trading at 34600, closing at the highs of the day, after selling down to lows of 34000. Q4 traded down to 34000, before late buying interest pushed the contract to close at 34500, up 300 on opening levels. The Cal27 strip featured a few times, between 28400-28500, and the Cal28 once at 24600.

PMX
The pmx market saw an early loss finding support into the close. July traded at 20,000. August was active between 19,150–19,650, with most activity around 19,300–19,500 before firming later in the session. HOLDING FIRM THROUGHOUT. NOPAC ENQUIRY CENTRED ON 5 AUG ONW LAYCANS. OWNERS OPENED THE WEEK TARGETING AROUND 18K BKI CJK WHILE CHARTERERS SAT PATIENTLY AT 15-16K BKI CJK, RESULTING IN VERY LITTLE LIQUIDITY. BY TUESDAY, BUSINESS WAS CONCLUDED AROUND 17K BKI CJK AND THOSE LEVELS HELD FOR THE BALANCE OF THE WEEK FOR THE SAME DATES. EAUS REMAINED FOCUSED ON THE HEAVY 1-10 AUG WINDOW WITH DEMAND DOMINATED BY CHINA, SOUTH KOREA, JAPAN AND SE ASIA REDELIVERY. INDIA CONTINUED TO SEE LITTLE INTEREST. THE WEEK OPENED WITH OWNERS OFFERING AROUND 18K BKI CJK AGAINST CHARTERERS BIDDING CLOSER TO 16.5K, BUT MOMENTUM QUICKLY SHIFTED AS CHINESE OPERATORS COMPETED AGGRESSIVELY FOR AVAILABLE TONNAGE, PUSHING FIXTURES INTO THE MID-HIGH 17'S BKI CJK. AS MORE BUSINESS WAS REPORTED AT THESE LEVELS, OWNERS BECAME INCREASINGLY BULLISH WITH OFFERS CLIMBING INTO THE VERY HIGH TEENS-20K BKI CJK WHILE CHARTERERS GENERALLY STARTED AROUND 17K. RUMOURS CIRCULATED OF 19K BKI CJK BEING ACHIEVED FOR THE 1-10 AUG WINDOW. DESPITE CHARTERERS POINTING TO THE GROWING LIST OF VESSELS OPEN 25-30 JUL, PARTICULARLY IN THE SOUTH, OWNERS REMAINED FIRMLY IN CONTROL AND SHOWED LITTLE SIGN OF SOFTENING FOR LATER DATES. EVEN WITH LIMITED INDIAN DEMAND, 17.5K BKI CJK WAS ACHIEVED FOR 1-10 AUG DATES (BHP) WITH SIMILAR LEVELS REPORTED FOR MID-AUG LAYCANS. INDO EXTENDED LAST FRIDAY'S RALLY WITH RATES CLIMBING A FURTHER 2-2.5K OVER THE WEEK AS TYPHOON BAVI-RELATED WEATHER DELAYS COMBINED WITH THE STRENGTH OF THE EAUS MARKET FORCING CHARTS WITH PROMPT CARGOES TO SECURE COVERAGE. THE WEEK OPENED WITH UNITS FIXING MID 16’S-17K BKI HK AND MOMENTUM CONTINUED WITH OA LMES CONCLUDED AROUND 16-17K DOP SOUTH CHINA, 19'S BKI HK EQUIV. SOME CHARTERERS LOOKED NORTH FOR ALTERNATIVE COVERAGE TO LIMIT HIGH HEADRATE EXPOSURE BUT THE STRONG BALLAST INCENTIVE CONTINUED TO DRAW MODERN KMX’S AWAY FROM THE PACIFIC. ALTHOUGH THE FORWARD TONNAGE LIST REMAINS RELATIVELY HEALTHY, PARTICULARLY FOR LATER DATES, OWNERS CONTINUE TO DICTATE PROCEEDINGS WITH CHARTERERS LARGELY WAITING IN THE HOPE OF A CORRECTION. sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize市场明显偏弱，C5西澳-青岛跌破12美元至11.70-11.75，太平洋成交稀薄，大矿商主导价格走向。Panamax大西洋近期货运仍偏紧挺，但5TC均值$20,236仅小幅下滑$80。Supramax亚洲航线成为亮点，11TC均值涨至$21,960。Handysize大西洋平稳，亚洲受台风影响船期延误偏紧。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 大船 bearish：C3跌$0.628至32.72，C5跌$0.585至11.805，8月期货32,200/32,400显示远月承压。Panamax neutral：5TC $20,236，Q3 26期货19,750/19,850相对僵持。Supramax bullish：11TC $21,960继续走强，亚洲需求稳健支撑。Handysize neutral：7TC $16,261太平洋略强。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注8月大船期货能否在32,000上方企稳，太平洋市场情绪仍脆弱。Panamax近月货盘支撑尚存，大西洋供给趋紧。Supramax关注南美及东南亚贸易流向，亚洲航线偏强格局或延续。
